201.h: The University of Ibadan, usually shortened to UI, is a federal university in Ibadan, the capital of Oyo State. It began in 1948 as University College, Ibadan, a college attached to the University of London, which meant its students sat London examinations and received London degrees. In 1962 it became an independent university able to award its own degrees, which makes it the oldest degree-awarding institution in Nigeria. For that reason it is often described as the country's premier university, and many later Nigerian universities were modelled on its structure.
201.a: UI is a large residential university with an enrolment of roughly 33,000 students across undergraduate and postgraduate programmes. Its long history means it has one of the widest ranges of established programmes in the country, including medicine through its teaching hospital links, sciences, humanities and social sciences.
201.c: The university is based in Ibadan, one of Nigeria's largest cities, in the south-west of the country.

202.h: The University of Lagos, known as UNILAG, is a public research university founded in 1962. It belongs to the group of first-generation Nigerian universities established in the years around independence, and it is regularly listed among the leading universities in Africa in international rankings.
202.a: UNILAG is one of the largest universities in the country. As of 2024 it was admitting about 8,500 undergraduates a year and had more than 57,000 students enrolled in total. Its College of Medicine trains doctors and other health professionals.
202.c: The university operates three campuses on the Lagos mainland. The main campus is at Akoka in Yaba, covers about 802 acres and is largely bordered by the Lagos Lagoon. A second, newer campus is also in Yaba, on the site of a former school of radiography, and the College of Medicine is at Idi-Araba in Surulere.

208.h: Abia State University, Uturu (ABSU) is a public university owned by the Abia State Government. It started in 1981 as Imo State University, founded by Sam Mbakwe while he was governor of the old Imo State, with its main campus at Etiti and its law department in Aba. In 1984 and 1985 the university moved to a permanent site at Uturu, near Okigwe. When Abia State was carved out of Imo State in 1991, the Uturu campus fell within the new state and became Abia State University.
208.a: As a state university, ABSU was set up to widen access to degree education for students in the region, and it offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
208.c: The main campus is at Uturu in Abia State, in south-eastern Nigeria.

209.h: Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University (ATBU) is a federal university of technology in Bauchi, in north-eastern Nigeria. It is named after Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa, Nigeria's first and only prime minister, and its motto, Doctrina Mater Artium, means that education is the mother of the practical arts. The institution was created in 1980 as the Federal University of Technology, Bauchi, and admitted its first pre-degree and remedial students in October 1981, with degree courses in science and science education starting a year later. In 1984 it was merged into Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, as its Bauchi campus, and it regained its independence in 1988, the year the National Universities Commission records for the present university.
209.a: ATBU's focus is technology, engineering and the sciences, in keeping with its origins as a university of technology.
209.c: The university is located in Bauchi, the capital of Bauchi State.

210.h: Achievers University is a private university in Owo, Ondo State. It grew out of the Achievers Group of Education and Training Organisation, an Ibadan-based education company, and was licensed in 2007. It began teaching in the 2007/2008 academic session and, by 2025, had graduated fourteen sets of students. The university is owned by its founder, Bode Ayorinde, together with a group of shareholders.
210.a: Achievers University is accredited by the National Universities Commission and runs undergraduate degree programmes.
210.c: The campus sits on land in the Idasen community of Owo, which takes in the Ulale, Ulema, Ijegunma, Isijogun and Amurin Elegba areas of the town.

211.h: Adamawa State University is a public university owned by the Adamawa State Government. It was established in 2002 under the Adamawa State University Law No. 10 of 2001, with the stated aim of supporting the development of the state.
211.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes for students from Adamawa State and beyond.
211.c: It is located in Mubi, in the northern senatorial district of Adamawa State, close to Nigeria's border with Cameroon.

212.h: Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko (AAUA) is a public university owned and run by the Ondo State Government. The National Universities Commission lists its year of establishment as 1999. It is named after Michael Adekunle Ajasin, a former governor of Ondo State.
212.a: AAUA offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes and is the main state-owned university serving Ondo State.
212.c: The university is located in the town of Akungba-Akoko in the Akoko area of northern Ondo State.

213.h: Adeleke University is a private university in Ede, Osun State, in south-western Nigeria. It was founded in 2011 by Chief Adedeji Adeleke through the Springtime Development Foundation, and it is part of the Seventh-day Adventist education system, which shapes its rules and campus culture.
213.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and is licensed by the National Universities Commission.
213.c: The campus is in Ede, a historic town in Osun State.

214.h: The African University of Science and Technology (AUST) is a private university in Abuja. It was founded in 2007 as the first campus of a planned pan-African network of science and technology institutes promoted by the Nelson Mandela Institution. From the start it concentrated on postgraduate training, and it recruits staff and students from across the continent, including African academics based abroad who teach as visiting professors.
214.a: AUST's programmes are concentrated in computer science and information technology management, materials science and engineering, petroleum engineering, pure and applied mathematics, and space and aerospace sciences, with a master's programme in public administration and policy. At its December 2022 graduation it awarded degrees to 145 people from 11 countries, 38 of them doctorates.
214.c: The university is located in Abuja, the Federal Capital Territory.

215.h: The Air Force Institute of Technology (AFIT) in Kaduna is a federal degree-awarding institution associated with the Nigerian Air Force. The National Universities Commission lists it among federal universities, with 2018 as its year of establishment.
215.a: AFIT offers undergraduate and postgraduate degrees, with a strong emphasis on engineering subjects relevant to aviation, such as mechanical and aeronautical engineering. The National Universities Commission has granted full accreditation to a number of its degree courses.
215.c: The institute is located in Kaduna, the capital of Kaduna State in north-western Nigeria.

216.h: Ajayi Crowther University (ACU) is a private, faith-based university in Oyo town, Oyo State. It is named after Samuel Ajayi Crowther, the nineteenth-century Yoruba clergyman who became the first African Anglican bishop. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2005.
216.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate degree programmes.
216.c: The campus is in the town of Oyo in Oyo State, south-western Nigeria.

217.h: Akwa Ibom State University (AKSU) is a public university owned by the Akwa Ibom State Government. It admitted its pioneer students in the 2010/2011 academic session, and the National Universities Commission lists 2010 as its year of establishment.
217.a: AKSU runs undergraduate and postgraduate programmes for students from the state and elsewhere in Nigeria.
217.c: The university's main campus is at Ikot Akpaden in Akwa Ibom State, in the Niger Delta region of south-southern Nigeria.

218.h: Al-Hikmah University is a private Islamic university in Ilorin, Kwara State. It was founded by the AbdulRaheem Oladimeji Islamic Foundation, based in Nigeria, together with the World Assembly of Muslim Youth, based in Jeddah. The Federal Government granted it an operating licence, number 010, on 7 January 2005, and it started teaching in the 2005/2006 session with 70 students across three colleges: Humanities, Management Sciences and Natural Sciences.
218.a: Al-Hikmah describes its goal as being a centre of intellectual and moral excellence, and it has grown well beyond its three founding colleges since 2005.
218.c: The university is located in Ilorin, the capital of Kwara State.

219.h: Al-Qalam University, Katsina (AUK), formerly Katsina University, is a private Islamic university established in 2005. It was the second private Islamic university to be licensed by the Federal Government of Nigeria.
219.a: The university is organised into colleges of social and management sciences, natural and applied sciences, education, humanities and postgraduate studies, together with a school of basic and remedial studies. It awards 22 undergraduate degrees, some available part-time as well as full-time, plus 11 master's and nine doctoral programmes, all accredited by the National Universities Commission.
219.c: The campus is on Dutsinma Road in Katsina, the capital of Katsina State.

220.h: Alex Ekwueme Federal University, Ndufu-Alike (AE-FUNAI) is a federal university founded in 2011, one of a group of new federal universities created that year to give each state a federal university. It is named after Alex Ekwueme, Nigeria's first executive vice-president.
220.a: AE-FUNAI offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes and describes research and innovation as central to its mission.
220.c: The university is at Ndufu-Alike in Ikwo, Ebonyi State, in south-eastern Nigeria.

221.h: Ambrose Alli University (AAU) is a state-owned university in Ekpoma, Edo State. It was founded by Ambrose Folorunsho Alli while he was governor of the old Bendel State, which later split into Edo and Delta States; the National Universities Commission records 1980, while other accounts give 1981. It was first called Bendel State University, then Edo State University, and was finally renamed in honour of its founder.
221.a: AAU is accredited by the National Universities Commission and runs a wide range of undergraduate and postgraduate programmes. Its library holds the university's information resources, and the university has invested in information technology for teaching and administration.
221.c: The university is located in Ekpoma, in the Esan area of Edo State.

222.h: The American University of Nigeria (AUN) is a private university in Yola, the capital of Adamawa State. Founded in 2003, it was the first university in sub-Saharan Africa to follow the American liberal arts model, and it describes itself as Africa's first development university, meaning it aims to help solve problems in the community around it.
222.a: AUN teaches at undergraduate, graduate and professional levels in an American-style curriculum, in which students take a broad range of courses alongside their major. It is a small university, with about 1,500 students and 93 academic staff, and it is accredited by the National Universities Commission.
222.c: The campus is in Yola, in north-eastern Nigeria.

223.h: Anchor University is a private Christian university owned by the Deeper Christian Life Ministry. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2016.
223.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and is licensed by the National Universities Commission.
223.c: The campus is at Ayobo, in the Ipaja area of Lagos State.

224.h: Arthur Jarvis University (AJU) is a private university founded in 2016. It was the first private university in Cross River State.
224.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and is licensed by the National Universities Commission.
224.c: It is located in Akpabuyo, near Calabar, the capital of Cross River State.

225.h: Augustine University is a private university established in 2015. It describes its mission as career-oriented education that combines personal development with technology, business and management.
225.a: The university runs undergraduate and postgraduate programmes with a practical, career-focused emphasis, organised in faculties that include a Faculty of Science.
225.c: The campus is at Ilara-Epe, in the Epe area of Lagos State.
